# Redcore · Brickmark

> Brickmark is a magnetic provenance assay for fired clay (batch provenance first; unit or course identity only if repeatability survives measurement). It is not a PUF and makes no security claims. The identity unit may be the course of four to eight bricks. Experiment 0 collects phone photos of twenty clay faces, named `{lot}-{nn}_r{rep}.jpg` and submitted as a GitHub issue. The v4 figures are MODEL ONLY; spectrum gate #3 is UNMEASURED.

The site (https://stevoblevo.github.io/redcore/) is a small game: ten quests ("bricks"), six rooms, and Tinder, a guide sprite. Everything an agent needs is in one fetch at [llms-full.txt](https://stevoblevo.github.io/redcore/llms-full.txt).


Site: https://stevoblevo.github.io/redcore/ · Repo: https://github.com/stevoblevo/redcore · Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stevoblevo/redcore/main/<path>

Rules for agents: quote numbers only as written here or in the repo; v4 numbers are MODEL ONLY; spectrum gate #3 is UNMEASURED; a phone photo is not a B-map; no PUF / crypto / security claims; saelion.co/field is lore, not a source.

## The ten steps (quests)
1. Ward (1050 °C · the kiln is hot): Safety: bricks are 2–3 kg. No glass table. Nothing goes in a fireplace.
2. Two hearths (choose your lots): Pick lots: Lot A = one stack / one store; Lot B = another if you can get it. Two lots make impostors honest.
3. Mark the end (pencil, never the face): Pencil the ID (e.g. A-01) on the end, not the scan face.
4. Find the shade (window light, no blown flash): Window light or shade. No flash if it blows the clay white.
5. First sight (capture 1 · _r1): Photograph twenty fired-clay faces — capture 1 (_r1). Fill the frame with clay texture, not room.
6. Second sight (capture 2 · _r2): Capture 2 (_r2) of every face — different lighting, day or operator if you can. Same phone is fine. Don't rotate 90° between reps unless you record it.
7. The square (about 5 × 5 cm): Crop about 5 × 5 cm of the same region. Don't invent a crop box — only pass --crop-box if you measured one.
8. Speak its name ({lot}-{nn}_r{rep}.jpg): Name every file {lot}-{nn}_r{rep}.jpg — use the Namer's Bench.
9. Hash receipt (optional · no EER) [optional side quest]: Optional: python protocol/optical_unit_identity.py --ingest path/to/A-01_r1.jpg (hash receipt, no EER).
10. Deliver (carry it to the assay): Submit: carry the course to the Assay, open the prefilled issue and attach your zip.

## Filename rules
- Pattern: `{lot}-{nn}_r{rep}.jpg`, e.g. `A-01_r1.jpg`
- lot: A or B (Lot A = one stack / one store; Lot B = another if you can get it)
- nn: face number 01–20, two digits
- rep: 1 or 2 (capture 1 and capture 2 of every face, different lighting, day or operator if possible)
- 20 faces total: A-01…A-10 and B-01…B-10, or one lot of 20; each photographed twice
- Pencil the ID on the end, never the scan face. Crop about 5 × 5 cm of the same region.

## How to submit
Open https://github.com/stevoblevo/redcore/issues/new?template=data-submission.md (label `data-submission`), fill it in, drag your zip of photos into the issue, then post. Or attach the zip on issue #11: https://github.com/stevoblevo/redcore/issues/11

## Notes / fails

## Every room, full text
Redcore · Brickmark · v0.3.1 · Room I · the Hearth

The brick remembers
where north was.

As fired clay cools, its magnetite locks a record of Earth's field (magnetite Curie temperature ≈580 °C; hematite Néel temperature ≈675 °C1,2). Brickmark asks whether that record, plus the clay's own texture, can tell one batch, and maybe one course, from another.

Your quest: lay a course of ten bricks with a phone and twenty clay faces, then deliver it to the assay. Tinder, the kiln sprite, will walk you there.

Light the kiln

⊕A provenance assay
Magnetic provenance for fired clay. Batch provenance first; spatial, unit or course identity only if repeatability survives measurement.

⊘Not a PUF
No PUF-as-crypto, no bed-face archive in a laid wall, no security language until repeatability is proven. The struck v1 claims stay dead.

▦The course is the unit
The identity unit may be the course of bricks: aggregate four to eight bricks for a usable identity length, if measured course BER earns it.

Before quoting numbers: the v4 figures (87 independent cells, 63 extractable bits per face) are MODEL ONLY simulation outputs, not measured. No bits-per-brick claim until the spectrum gate (issue #3) runs.

docs/SAELION_REALITY_PROGRAM.md §1, §2.2, WP4 · briefs/v3.md · briefs/v4.md

Room II · the Course · Experiment 0 · $0 · a phone

Lay the course. Ten bricks, ten sigils.

Each quest is a brick. Tap a brick to fire it: it cools past 675 °C, then 580 °C, its needle locks north, and it is laid into your course. Tap a laid brick again to lift it. Progress stays in this browser. Optical unit identity, complementary to the magnetic Afternoon Zero. Source: experiment0_optical.md, experiment0_ingest.md.

Break the course (reset)

Room III · the Namer's Bench · pattern {lot}-{nn}_r{rep}.jpg

Stamp a name into the clay.

Controls: lot (A or B), face number (1–20), capture (r1 or r2). The tablet shows the resulting name, e.g. A-01_r1.jpg; tap to copy. A details panel lists the full shot list for the chosen lot.

Room IV · the Three Pillars · quoted from the repo only

Three separate stones. Never merge them.

⋮1 · Scan pitch
Spectrum gate (issue #3): scan a defined patch at 0.25–0.5 mm pitch.
issue #3 · docs/SAELION_REALITY_PROGRAM.md

⇕2 · Standoff (height) tolerance
Derived jig spec: standoff repeatability ≤ 0.2 mm (alongside lateral ≤ 0.25 mm, σB/n ≥ 10).
briefs/v4.md · briefs/v3.md

∿3 · v4 error budget MODEL ONLY
0.25 mm lateral, 0.1 mm standoff, σB/n = 10, BER ~5% (executed run: BER 6.12%, 63 bits; 87 cells at 3 mm cell pitch, 1 mm standoff).
briefs/v4.md · cuda/results/ASSAY_v4_run.md

Room V · Spectrum Gate #3 · UNMEASURED

The gate is a low-pass filter. Turn the dial.

Model: grain-scale magnetization is roughly uncorrelated, so the field at standoff h is that source upward-continued, multiplied in the Fourier domain by exp(−2πkh). Standoff is the low-pass filter; cutoff wavelength ≈ 2πh.

Spatial frequency k = 0.50 cycles/mm (wavelength 2.00 mm)
Curve is the model exp(−2πkh) only, with no data. Dots mark the gate's four standoffs (0.5 / 1 / 2 / 5 mm). Slider is illustrative, not a measured spectrum.

The gate: on one strong face, scan at 0.25–0.5 mm pitch, repeat at 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 5 mm standoff, and compare measured B-maps' height attenuation against exp(−2πkh). If the measured spectrum is much redder, the unit assay may be dead.

Controls: empty-jig scan, same scan twice without remount, scan after remount, magnetic-sheet control. A phone photo is not a B-map and does not touch this gate. Issue #3: https://github.com/stevoblevo/redcore/issues/3

briefs/v4.md §1 · briefs/v3.md · docs/SAELION_REALITY_PROGRAM.md · cuda/python/postprocess.py

Room VI · the Assay · deliver your course

Carry the course to the assay.

Write the course's label, then deliver it. A prefilled GitHub issue opens; drag your zip of photos into it before posting. No git needed.

Fields: lots; faces photographed; lighting / reps; notes (weathered, painted, fails…). The "Deliver to the assay" button opens a prefilled GitHub issue.

Prefer the existing thread? Attach the zip on issue #11.

Redcore · github.com/stevoblevo/redcore · v0.4.0 · previous builds: v0.3.1 · v0.3.0 · v0.2.1 · Publish the fail if it fails.

## The North That Was (v0.4.0 adventure; lore + model, no measured data)
Entered from the ↟ door in the room map or the Hearth ("Walk The North That Was"); deep links #north and #north=<station>. A journey along one glowing magnetic field line, following one brick's life. Tinder leads. Each station has a glyph: ∴ △ ↟ ▦ ◷ ∿ ⊙.
1. ∴ The Clay Pit: wet clay with random magnetite and hematite grains; stirring only swirls them, so there is no north. (Picture of the idea, not a simulation.)
2. △ The Kiln: fire to 1050 °C (the site's illustrative firing peak); every grain's moment flips freely and old directions are wiped.
3. ↟ The Cooling: below the hematite Néel temperature ≈675 °C and the magnetite Curie temperature ≈580 °C (Dunlop & Özdemir 1997; Butler 1992) grains freeze in a slight preference for Earth's field: "the north that was". Drag the compass onto the brick to see it lock (it spins if still above 580 °C). Alignment is exaggerated and the direction is illustrative, not a measured declination.
4. ▦ The Course: one brick gives one noisy arrow; laid with neighbours, the pattern across the course is the candidate identity, only if measured course BER earns it. Visual only; it does not change saved quest progress.
5. ◷ The Long Years (lore): a time-lapse of seasons and centuries over the wall. The arrows are drawn unchanged; the effect of weathering on remanence is not measured.
6. ∿ The Reader: a scanner at standoff h; each spatial frequency k fades as exp(−2πkh) (synthetic source, model curve). Whether real bricks survive this is spectrum gate #3, UNMEASURED (issue #3).
7. ⊙ The Ask: "You can help: photograph a face." Leads into the quest course (Room II).
Side paths (unsealed by play): ≡ The Tablet (decorative wedge marks; lore, not a real inscription or translation; unsealed by stirring the pit), ✧ The Wanderer (Ash, Tinder's ash cousin; unsealed after centuries pass), § The Scroll (lore verse "The kiln forgets, the cooling chooses, the wall keeps, the reader asks."; unsealed after one scanner pass). Each holds a sigil; the hidden-sigil counter is now 8 (five in the rooms, three on side paths).

## Autoplay (v0.4.0)
A ▶ toggle in the top bar, on the Hearth, and in the adventure, or the deep link #autoplay. It visits every room, opens one repo doc in the tablet reader, then walks every station and side path, demoing the stir, firing, cooling, compass lock, laying the course, the time-lapse and the scanner, with Tinder's captions and a progress bar; it ends at The Ask (about 73 s). Click or Space pauses/resumes, Esc stops, ⏭ skips a step. It never writes saved quest progress or sigils.
